meta.title_bilingual: 【原水水质与加酸中和 (Base Water & Acid Neutralisation)】
meta.source: Van der Lugt, G. et al. (2020) Nutrient Solutions for Greenhouse Crops, Version 4, ISBN 9789464021844. Eurofins Agro / Nouryon / SQM / Yara.

quality_levels.suitability_en: Not suitable when recirculation is necessary
quality_levels.suitability_zh: 需要循环回用时不适用

quality_levels.suitability_en: Not to be used for salt-sensitive crops

iron_limits_umol_l.note: Base-water Fe is NEVER credited as nutrient; it precipitates at the emitter (p.13-14).

hco3_safety_buffer_mmol_l.rationale: Retaining 0.5-0.75 mmol/L HCO3 buffers pH to 5.5-6.0. Neutralising all of it drops irrigation pH below 5 (p.24).

neutralisation.constraint: Acid anions count against the recipe: nitric is capped by NO3 headroom, phosphoric by P headroom.
neutralisation.co2_requirement: The reaction must occur in an OPEN system so CO2 can escape, otherwise pH will not fall.

dosing_bases.stock_tank: kg per 1000 L at 100x = mmol/L * MW * 0.1
dosing_bases.working_solution: L per 1000 L at 1x = (mmol/L / 1000 * V) / molarity
dosing_bases.warning: Confusing the two is a 100x dosing error.

nutrient_deduction_rules.clamping: Credits are capped at the recipe target; base water carrying more of an ion than the target cannot be un-supplied, so the excess is reported, not negated.

spec_divergences.basis: WUR Table 5, p.26 lists exactly these three acid grades. Neither 65% HNO3 nor 85% H3PO4 appears in the manual.
spec_divergences.resolution: Exported the catalogue grades. Molarity is computed from density and mass-per-mole-of-H+, so a site using a different grade can add it to the catalogue and every downstream figure follows.
spec_divergences.severity: material - dosing volumes differ by roughly 1.7x between 38% and 65% nitric acid
